item.title: Nested query
item.description:
Nested query #

Matches parent documents whose nested sub-documents — objects mapped with "nested": true — satisfy a query within one element at a time. It exists because a flattened object index cannot keep two field values inside the same array element together — the pitfall the next section makes concrete.

The cross-element problem #

A flattened index correlates across array elements, not within them: variants.color = blue AND variants.size = L matches a document as soon as some element is blue and some element is L — not necessarily the same one. item.title: Join query
item.description:
Join query #

Status: functional (semi-join). Joins need a running node — the gateway orchestrates and the engine executes, which is why the wasm playground does not host them. The joins tutorial walks the complete relational sequence — references → join → FK-routed writes → salting → ?routing= addressing — step by step against a live node.

item.title: Traverse query
item.description:
Traverse query #

Term and full-text queries match document content; none of them can ask “what is connected to these documents?” — the question citation graphs, reference data and knowledge graphs are made of. The traverse query answers it: a bounded graph traversal over a relation-typed edge field — starting from seed documents, walk the edges up to max_depth hops and emit every reached node as a hit.

Scores encode distance — 1.0 / (1.0 + depth) — so seeds outrank 1-hop neighbors, which outrank 2-hop neighbors, and the standard top-K collector orders the results.

item.title: Graph projection block
item.description:
Graph projection block #

Add a graph block to any search request and the response carries a graph — nodes and edges — built from the hit set, alongside the normal hits. Where the traverse query searches by walking edges, the graph block renders: it takes the documents a query already found and projects them into a node/edge structure a UI (or a GraphRAG pipeline) can consume directly.
